chunks: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from al-'Abbas, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mughirah, from Mu'awiyah ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I asked Aba 'Abd Allah عليه السلام about a man who had a nocturnal emission, then when he awoke he found only a small amount of moisture. He said: “It is nothing, unless he is ill, for then he becomes weakened; in that case ghusl is obligatory upon him.”

key_terms.احْتَلَمَ: experienced a nocturnal emission in sleep
key_terms.الْغُسْلُ: ritual bath required for purification from janabah
key_terms.بَلَلًا: moisture or wetness found upon waking
key_terms.مَرِيضًا: ill or sick, affecting the legal ruling here
key_terms.يَضْعُفُ: becomes weak, indicating weakness due to illness

ai.seo_question: Does a small amount of moisture after a nocturnal emission require ghusl?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about ghusl after experiencing a nocturnal emission and then finding only a small amount of moisture upon waking. The Imam عليه السلام states that such slight moisture does not require ghusl in general, except in the case of illness, where weakness may affect the emission and ghusl becomes obligatory.
